main_issue: Whether alcohol is served at the shared housewarming given D's religious discomfort as co-host, versus A's purchase and B's invited colleagues.

A-B.evidence: A cites B's invited colleagues (T10) and asks B if he wants to send guests to a bar (T12); B refuses (T13). Both want alcohol served.

A-C.evidence: C proposes serving alcohol self-service (T6, T8), then a balcony cooler (T16) which keeps A's drinks in use; A doesn't reply, but C's position fits A's.

A-D.evidence: A: 'I've already bought all this, I can't return it' (T10) and rejects D's alcohol-free idea (T12); D keeps objecting (T7, T9); D says 'we need to figure this out' (T15).

B-C.evidence: C offers a solution where B's colleagues 'can still get a drink' (T16); B had wanted drinks (T5) and C backed having both (T6).

B-D.evidence: B says 'That's a bit of a problem' (T5) and rejects D's bar suggestion: 'I can't do that' (T13); D proposed an alcohol-free party (T11).

C-D.evidence: C probes D's feelings (T8) and proposes a balcony cooler for D (T16); D agrees 'We need to figure this out' (T15) but hasn't accepted the cooler.
